name: Collage
source: A maximalist pile: die-cut stickers with a white border and a shadow slapped on at angles, torn paper, tape, halftone and hand lettering, overlapping on a scrapbook layout and wobbling on twos. Described from the atlas sticker and collage entries; no art is carried.

frame_device.what: A paper, cardboard or grid-paper ground that fills up with overlapping stickers, scraps and tape; the pile grows through the film and the sticker slap is the film's heartbeat.
frame_device.moves: One new sticker slaps on every beat from an edge with a rotation, a shadow that tightens as it sticks; the pile boils on twos; the camera pans over the pile and punches into one sticker for each idea.

ground_motion: The whole pile wobbles +-1 degree on 8 fps held frames and the paper drifts in tone; the camera creeps 2 percent across the pile so it is never still.

type.classes: A heavy display face for sticker words, hand-cut or marker lettering for labels, a small mono for tags; text sits in stickers and on tape strips.
type.behaviour: Words are stickers that slap on and stay; a changing word is a new sticker on the same spot; readable at rest, never hidden under a new sticker for more than 0.4 s.

image.treatment: Cut-out Codex or photo subjects with a white die-cut border and a soft shadow, graded to one palette; halftone and torn-paper scraps as fillers; the product UI is a sticker-framed screen.
image.behaviour: Stickers arrive with scale, spin and a landing bounce; the pile is re-ordered by lifting stickers; images are reused 3 or more times at different scales.

transitions: sticker slap covers the frame, the next scene is under it
peel: the top layer curls away to the next layer
scrapbook camera punch into one sticker

techniques.name: Sticker slap
techniques.what: A die-cut sticker arrives oversize and spinning, lands, bounces and sticks.
techniques.route: RasanSticker.slap(tl, s, {at, from: 'top', duration: 0.38}); the shadow tightens on the landing frame.

techniques.name: Scrapbook pile
techniques.what: A seeded scatter of stickers, scraps and tape fills the frame with deliberate overlaps.
techniques.route: RasanSticker.scrapbook(stage, items, {seed, area, tape: 3}) then slapAll(tl, items, {at, every: 0.22}).

techniques.name: Pile boil
techniques.what: The whole pile trembles by a hair on held frames.

techniques.name: Sticker word swap
techniques.what: A new sticker slaps onto the old word's spot to change it.
techniques.route: slap a text sticker over the previous one at the same x, y with from: 'none' (scale 1.6 to 1, spin 12).

techniques.name: Camera punch
techniques.what: The camera snaps into one sticker for the beat's idea, then pulls back to the pile.
techniques.route: Scale and translate the pile container to one item (2.2x), 0.5 s power3.inOut, hold, back out.

techniques.name: Tape and scrap
techniques.what: Tape strips and torn paper land under and over stickers to build depth.
techniques.route: RasanSticker.tape / scrap placed at item corners; slide in 0.2 s with a 2 degree settle.

techniques.name: Halftone grade
techniques.what: Photos run through one halftone or gradient map to sit in the same pile.
techniques.route: art.mjs treat --op halftone or gradient-map on every photo; riso offset by a 3 px misregistration on the overlay.

techniques.name: Peel away
techniques.what: The top layer peels off to the next scene.
techniques.route: Top layer clip-path corner curl (polygon animating) with a gradient shadow strip, 0.5 s power2.in; next layer beneath.

techniques.name: Word choreography
techniques.what: Each word of a line enters from its own place and settles into the line with a lift; the key word last with a little more overshoot.
techniques.route: RasanShape.split(el, {by: 'words'}) on label text; each word slaps in as its own small sticker from its own angle (rotation +-14, scale 1.4 to 1), 0.35 s, stagger 0.08 s, key word last.

signature: The last sticker is the product's name slapped square in the middle of the finished pile, and the pile freezes mid-wobble.

density.note: A new sticker or camera punch every 0.4 to 0.8 s; layers at the peak: 8 to 14 (ground, scraps, tape, 4 to 8 stickers, label, product plate).

palette.note: A brand palette picks 3 to 4 sticker colours; the white border and the shadow stay.

do: Give every sticker a white die-cut border and a shadow
Slap one new thing per beat from an edge with rotation
Grade all photos to one palette
Reuse each cut-out 3 or more times
dont: Do not use rectangular photos without a cut-out or frame
Do not hide the claim under a later sticker
Do not use smooth easing on the wobble
Do not leave the frame empty; it is a maximalist film
